GC.01.stem: Which idea from John Locke did the American colonists rely on most directly to justify self-government?

choices.text: Natural rights that government exists to protect
The divine right of kings to rule alone
The economic theory of laissez-faire markets
The military duty of every free citizen

GC.01.reteach: Re-anchor on Locke's Second Treatise; re-teach natural rights + social contract.

distractor_tags.label: B
distractor_tags.rationale: Documented misconception: divine right of kings is the opposite of Locke's consent-based theory.

distractor_tags.label: C
distractor_tags.rationale: Prior-knowledge error: confuses Enlightenment economic theory (laissez-faire) with Locke's political rights theory.

distractor_tags.label: D
distractor_tags.rationale: Prior-knowledge error: confuses classical/republican civic duty with Locke's natural-rights basis.

GC.01.key_rationale: Locke's natural-rights theory holds that government exists to protect pre-existing rights, which colonists used to justify governing themselves.
GC.01.dok_rationale: Requires connecting a philosopher's concept to its political purpose (explain how), which is basic reasoning rather than simple recall.
GC.01.blooms_rationale: Student constructs meaning by relating Locke's idea to the colonists' justification, an Understand-level task.
